note: Rarity is varied by subsampling the target class in the training set only; the test set is identical across all conditions. Note that subsampling also lowers the local density of the class, so the overlap measured at small n is not comparable with the overlap measured on the full class; the measured_N3 column records this rather than holding it fixed. Overlap is varied by blending every point of the target class a fraction alpha towards a randomly matched point of its nearest competing class. The class frequency is identical at every level. The blend contracts the class's own variance by up to a quarter, which is reported as a confound rather than corrected: it makes the class easier, so it works against an observed decline in F1, and correcting it by per-feature rescaling was tried and found to destroy the manipulation (see blend_class_towards). The pool of partner points is drawn from the training split and the same pool is used for the training and the test split, so both are mapped into the same region of feature space and the resulting drop in F1 reflects class overlap rather than a train/test mismatch. Partner classes below --min_partner_rows are not eligible, because drawing with replacement from a small pool breaks the target class into tight internally-pure knots and lowers the measured overlap. Overlap is re-measured at every level so the manipulation is verified rather than assumed.
